identity.title: CO excitation in the Seyfert galaxy NGC 7130
identity.journal: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society

paper_type_evidence.quote: For details on the analysis of the ALMA data we refer to Zhao et al. (2016); here we only remind the points which are relevant for our analysis.

evidence.quote: NGC7130 is a local ( _z_ =0.0161) Luminous Infrared Galaxy

question.value: What is the impact of AGN activity (X-ray heating) on the molecular gas in NGC7130, as probed by modelling its CO SLED with PDR and XDR models?

evidence.quote: The goal of this letter is to definitively assess the impact of the AGN activity on the molecular gas in NGC7130.
The ALMA observations have been performed in Cycle 2 (project 2013.1.00524.S, PI: Nanyao Lu)

evidence.quote: The yellow triangle represent the new ALMA CO(6-5) data from Zhao et al. (2016).

analysis_steps.goal: Fit X-ray spectrum for AGN luminosity

method.value: Joint Chandra+NuSTAR fit with mekal thermal components and MYTorus

evidence.quote: To achieve these goals, we used the MYTorus model (Murphy & Yaqoob 2009)

key_parameters.value: photon index fixed to 1.9; NH and inclination free

evidence.quote: While the photon index was fixed to 1.9, as typically observed in AGN and quasars
This overall modelling provides a _χ_ [2] /dof (degrees of freedom) of 99.1/85

validation.value: Compared with Koss et al. (2016) and Ricci et al. (2017)

evidence.quote: Our results are in good agreement with the analysis of the hard-X ray data

analysis_steps.goal: Compute PDR and XDR CO emissivity grids

method.value: 1-D constant-density slab CLOUDY runs; PDR with Starburst99 SED, XDR with table AGN

evidence.quote: we run two sets of CLOUDY models that assume the molecular clouds to be a 1-D gas slab with constant density located at a fixed distance _d_ from the source

key_parameters.value: PDR: log n=2-4.5, d=75-250 pc; XDR: log n=3.5-5.5; max log NH=23

assumptions.value: Salpeter IMF 1-100 Msun, solar metallicity, aox=-1.4, Tcut=1e6 K

evidence.quote: The ratio of the UV and X-ray continua ( _a_ _ox_ ) is fixed to _−_ 1 _._ 4

analysis_steps.goal: Fit CO SLED with three components

method.value: chi2 minimisation with 9 free parameters (density, radiation field, normalisation per component)

evidence.quote: We find the best fit by a _χ_ [2] minimitation routine with 9 free parameters

key_parameters.value: NH ~1e22 cm-2 for PDRs, ~1e23 for XDR

evidence.quote: We fix the column density _N_ _H_ _∼_ 10 [22] cm _[−]_ [2] for the PDRs and _N_ _H_ _∼_ 10 [23] cm _[−]_ [2] for XDR.

fitting.value: 1 sigma from Delta chi2=3.5 marginalising over other parameters

evidence.quote: considering a ∆ _χ_ [2] =3.5 (see Lampton et al. 1976)

analysis_steps.goal: Derive cold gas mass and alpha_CO

method.value: alpha_CO = Mcold/LCO using observed CO(1-0) luminosity

evidence.quote: the estimated gas mass allow us to estimate directly the CO-to-H 2 conversion factor

validation.value: Compared with MW and ULIRG values

evidence.quote: The value found is consistent with the overall properties of NGC7130 being a LIRG galaxy hosting a moderate, obscured AGN.
We model the CO SLED using the version c13.03 of the photoionization/photodissociation code CLOUDY
The SED is obtained with the stellar population synthesis code Starburst99
to apply _χ_ [2] statistics within the xspec package (Arnaud 1996)
Data were reprocessed and screened using standard settings and the nupipeline task
The total line flux is 1230 _±_ 74 Jy km s _[−]_ [1]
The intrinsic 2–10 keV and 1–100 keV luminosities of the AGN are 1 _._ 6 _×_ 10 [43] erg s _[−]_ [1] and 5 _._ 1 _×_ 10 [43] erg s _[−]_ [1], respectively.
We obtain an equatorial column density of (5 _._ 3 _±_ 1 _._ 6) _×_ 10 [24] cm _[−]_ [2] and _θ_ _obs_ = 79 _±_ 5 degrees.
The total cold gas mass necessary to fit the CO observation is _M_ _cold_ _∼_ 10 [9] _M_ _⊙_
that implies a CO-to-H2 conversion factor _α_ _CO_ =1.1 M _⊙_ pc _[−]_ [2] K km s _[−]_ [1]

findings_qualitative.value: PDR models reproduce CO up to J~6 but not higher J; an XDR component is needed.

evidence.quote: We find that PDRs can reproduce the CO lines up to J _∼_ 6, however, the higher rotational ladder requires the presence of a separate source of excitation.

claims.hypothesis: PDRs alone can reproduce the CO SLED
claims.experiment: CLOUDY PDR grids compared with CO(5-4)/(4-3) and CO(10-9)/(5-4) ratios
claims.result: PDR reproduces the CO(5-4)/(4-3) ratio but not CO(10-9)/(5-4)
claims.finding: An additional high-J excitation source is needed

evidence.quote: These parameter ranges, typical of PDRs, do not reproduce the observed CO(10-9)/CO(5-4) ratio.

claims.hypothesis: AGN X-ray heating explains the high-J CO
claims.result: XDR at 250 pc, log n=3.5, T~100 K fits the SLED
claims.finding: XDR heating by the Compton-thick AGN is favoured over shocks

evidence.quote: We consider X-ray heating by the AGN as a source of excitation, and find that it can reproduce the observed CO Spectral Energy Distribution.

why_this_method.value: Shocks are judged unlikely given the observed LCO/LFIR ratio.

evidence.quote: A chemistry driven by shocks (scenario (b), supported by Pereira-Santaella et al. 2014) is unlikely given the observed _L_ _CO_ _/L_ _IR_ ratio.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Shock heating rejected based on LCO/LFIR ~1.5e-4 typical of XDR/PDR

evidence.quote: NGC7130 has an observed _L_ _CO_ _/L_ _F IR_ ratio _∼_ 1 _._ 5 _×_ 10 _[−]_ [4], a factor typical of XDR/PDR models

referee_caveats_inferred: Nine-parameter fit to ~11 integrated CO points is degenerate; no goodness-of-fit stated
ALMA used as a single flux and size constraint, and single-dish fluxes cover a larger area
Shocks excluded by one ratio argument only
